page: Amazon Web Services r8i.32xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical Intel Xeon 6975P-C cores running at 3.9 GHz, with 480 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, but offers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 10%. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers top-tier read bandwidth, reaching 10218.84 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 383.47 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to top-tier prompt processing speeds for large language models, such as 42.57 tokens/sec on a 70B model.

Given its high memory density and strong multi-threaded capabilities, this server is optimized for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. It is highly suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching platforms like Redis—where it achieves 218.29 million operations per second—and CPU-based machine learning inference. The absence of local storage means workloads rely on network-attached storage, while the high-density DDR5 memory configuration offers a resource-dense profile for consolidated virtualization and memory-bound enterprise applications.
